# Summary of the 2017 Electoral Manifesto

## Core Themes

This manifesto centers on withdrawal from the European Union and establishing independent governance. The document outlines six key tests for a successful departure: full legal sovereignty, complete migration control, restoration of maritime rights including a 200-mile exclusive economic zone, independent trade capabilities, no financial divorce settlement, and completion by end of 2019.

## Economic Policy

The fiscal plan proposes £35 billion in savings through reducing overseas aid from 0.7% to 0.2% of Gross National Income, cancelling the HS2 rail project, reforming funding allocation formulas, and ending EU contributions. Key spending priorities include:

- **Taxation**: Raising the income tax threshold to £13,500, increasing the 40% rate threshold to £55,000, and raising inheritance tax thresholds to £500,000 per individual
- **Business**: Cutting business rates by 20% for premises under £50,000 rateable value, scrapping quarterly tax returns for the self-employed
- **Cost of living**: Removing VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaway food, abolishing the television licence fee

## Public Services

### Healthcare
The manifesto commits an additional £11 billion annually to health and social care by 2022, including:
- Lifting medical school caps from 7,500 to 10,000 places
- Increasing nurse training placements
- £500 million annually for mental health services
- Integration of health and social care systems
- Restricting non-urgent NHS access to British citizens or those with five years of tax contributions

### Education
Proposals include reintroducing grammar schools nationwide, establishing vocational training similar to German models, abolishing tuition fees for science and medical students who work domestically post-graduation, and restoring maintenance grants.

### Housing
A Housing Development Corporation would oversee factory-built modular homes, targeting up to 100,000 affordable homes annually for first-time buyers under 40, priced under £100,000.

## Immigration and Integration

The manifesto proposes reducing net migration to zero over five years through:
- An Australian-style points-based system
- A five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration after EU withdrawal
- Requiring five years of tax contributions before benefit eligibility
- Testing social attitudes of applicants regarding core values

On integration, proposals include disbanding religious councils operating parallel legal systems, banning face coverings in public, increased prosecution of practices like female genital mutilation, and school inspections addressing extremism concerns.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

Military spending would increase to a genuine 2% of GDP plus £1 billion annually, including:
- 20,000 additional armed forces personnel
- 7,000 more prison officers, 20,000 more police officers, 4,000 border staff
- A dedicated naval hospital ship
- Maintaining nuclear deterrent

A new Veterans Administration would provide consolidated support services, and legislation would protect former service members from historical prosecution.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposed changes include:
- Abolishing the House of Lords
- Creating an English Parliament with 375 members
- Halving House of Commons membership to 325
- Introducing proportional representation
- Enabling binding citizen-initiated referenda
- Restricting postal voting to demonstrated necessity

## Environmental and Energy Policy

The manifesto proposes repealing the 2008 Climate Change Act, withdrawing from the Paris Agreement, supporting diverse energy sources including shale gas exploration, and protecting ancient woodlands through enhanced planning restrictions.

## Fishing and Coastal Regeneration

Central to the post-EU vision is reclaiming maritime zones, leaving the Common Fisheries Policy, withdrawing from the 1964 London Convention, and creating coastal enterprise zones with enhanced business rate relief and housing improvement powers.
